units.position: Cumberland's region metres: centre (0, 0), 760 x 560 m (x -380..380, y -280..280); x metres east, y metres north, both ground metres
units.world: in the game's world units (ADR 0034) x is the same and a metre of ground northward is 0.643 of a unit (world y = 0.643 x y); every y in this file is ground metres, and so are heights and sizes

offset.rule: Nine Mile Creek's metres: x_nmc = x + 0, y_nmc = y + 560. Cumberland's south edge (y -280) is Nine Mile Creek's north edge (y 280); the two frames' x ranges are the same, so Cumberland's column c is Nine Mile Creek's column c

units.height: metres about mean sea level; spring low -2.20, neap low -0.99, mean 0, neap high +0.99, spring high +2.20
units.profile: cross-shore profiles are [distance from the reference line in metres, + inland, elevation in metres]; a section runs along the line from its from point to its to point (from_s, to_s: metres along the smoothed line)
units.slope: a slope 1:n is n metres across for every metre of rise
units.texture: ground/CumberlandSeabed_HeightTex_plan.png: 16-bit grey, 1520 x 1120, 2 texels a metre, texel (col, row) from the top-left centred at x = -380 + (col + 0.5) / 2, y = 280 - (row + 0.5) / 2; height = -6 + 12 x code / 65535. ground/CumberlandSeabed_StillTex_plan.png: the still water on the same scale, code 0 = none (filter the codes, then decode: ADR 0046 s5)
units.boats: a boat lies wherever the water over the bed is deeper than her draught (the brief, section 3: a standing ruling, never a rule). A berth's bed is the shallowest on its keel line (for slips, on every slip's); afloat_from = bed + draught; way_in_from = the least bed on the best way in from the open sea + draught; springs and neaps = the share of a spring (amplitude 2.2) or neap (0.99) tide's cycle when both hold
units.checkpoints: checkpoints: plan (the design height where the plan sets one, else the composer's ground before encoding) against texture (the height texture read bilinear at the point, the game's read), within tol metres; the seam's are Nine Mile Creek's row 0 against Cumberland's row 1119 read along the row, tol 0. stillpoints: the planned still-water level against the still texture's texel nearest the point, within tol

sections.name: the marina shore
sections.type: a stony shore under a low bank: the marina's bulkhead and apron
sections.why: The natural shore under the marina, steeper than the beach: the basin is dredged off it and the apron filled over it to a bulkhead at y -126.

sections.name: the marina point
sections.type: a low point of sandstone ledges under a bank 3 m tall
sections.why: A blunt low point, 56 m across, running 65 m south from the shore, its top a flat bank: it shelters the marina from the east, and the breakwater runs west from its west face. Pass B eased the bank (4.6 m to 2.0 m over 6 m, no steeper than 1 in 2.3) so no texel steps more than half a metre on it.

sections.name: the peninsula shore

water.rule: the water's shapes in plan order: the marina's basin and approach dredged, then the breakwater and the jetty built over them

shapes.name: the marina basin
shapes.why: Dredged to the floor, -6.0, between the bulkhead (y -126) and the breakwater; its side slopes 1 in 3. The bulkhead's face holds the dredge back at y -126, and the jetty holds it back on the west (x 179, under the jetty's crest): the resort beach west of the jetty keeps its own slope.

shapes.name: the marina's mouth and approach
shapes.why: The mouth between the jetty's head and the breakwater's, dredged to -6.0 and out south-west to the bay's own floor.

shapes.name: the breakwater
shapes.why: A rubble mound from the marina point's west face, curving west 85 m: its crest at +3.6 (1.4 m over the spring high), its sides 1 in 1.5 to the floor. It shelters the basin from the south.

shapes.name: the jetty
shapes.why: A short rubble jetty on the basin's west side, between the marina and the resort beach: it closes the basin from the west and leaves the mouth facing south-west. Its root meets the apron at the apron's height (+3.4) and its crest falls to +3.0 at its head.

calls.lean: north of the road: holes 1 to 4 whole, the 5th's tee and the 18th's approach and green, the clubhouse across the road from the resort's gate; holes 5 to 17 run east past the edge along Rocky Point. It reads as a course by its tees, mown fairways, greens with flags, bunkers, three ponds and the cart path
options: holes 1 to 4, the 5th tee and the 18th green in frame, north of the road: the lean
the course wrapped round the resort, between the road and the shore
a compressed nine-hole course wholly in frame
